title: Hot dog sandwich, meat and poultry, on white bread

content.title: About
content.content: A hot dog sandwich consists of a boiled or grilled meat‑and‑poultry sausage placed between two slices of soft white bread. It is often served with mustard, ketchup, mayonnaise and pickles.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first hot‑dog recipe appeared in the United States in the late 19th century.
In Russia the sandwich gained popularity in the 1990s alongside the rise of fast‑food chains.
White bread gives a neutral base that lets the sausage flavor shine.
There are many variations of the filling, from classic beef to turkey and chicken.
The hot dog is a cultural icon of street food and sporting events.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Meat and poultry sausage provides complete proteins essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Animal proteins are rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The product supplies B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Combining carbohydrates from the bread with fats and proteins from the sausage quickly replenishes energy stores.

items.title: Convenient snack
items.content: Easy to transport and eat on the go, making it a practical quick meal.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Processed sausages often contain a lot of salt, which can raise blood pressure if consumed frequently.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Meat sausages may be high in saturated fat, contributing to elevated cholesterol levels.

items.title: Allergy to additives
items.content: Some sausages include preservatives and flavor enhancers that can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Gluten in bread
items.content: White bread contains gluten, making the sandwich unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The sandwich can be calorie‑rich, so portion control is advisable for weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The hot dog is easy to hold in one hand. It can be warmed in a microwave or on a grill, and topped with sauces, fresh vegetables, cheese or pickles to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the assembled sandwich in the refrigerator for up to 2 days in an airtight container. Store the sausage separately at 0 °C–4 °C. If frozen, it can last up to 1 month, though the bread quality may decline.
